papers.title: Ultrasonic fatigue response of vertically and horizontally printed Ti-6al-4v and Inconel 718
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effect of build orientation (vertical vs. horizontal) on the me-chanical behaviour and ultrasonic fatigue testing (UFT) performance of additively manufac-tured Ti‑6Al‑4V and Inconel 718 specimens. Additive manufacturing (AM) is known to introduce anisotropic microstructures, with orientation, defects, and process conditions sig-nificantly influencing fatigue strength [1]. In particular, layer orientation affects both ten-sile and fatigue properties [2]. Five specimens per alloy were produced in each orientation and tested using UFT at 20 kHz. System calibration was supported by Digital Image Corre-lation (DIC) and laser measurements to reduce data scatter in the high-cycle regime [3]. Mechanical properties including Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratio, and stress–strain re-sponse were determined for both orientations. Combining Finite Element Analysis (FEA), DIC, and analytical/statistical methods enhanced confidence in interpreting deformation and stress behaviour. Results showed orientation-dependent differences. Horizontally built specimens generally exhibited longer fatigue lives and greater stiffness along the loading axis, consistent with prior findings [2]. While the combined methods were effective in as-sessing global stress behaviour, further work is needed to resolve layer-induced effects con-tributing to anisotropy.

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to investigate the effect of build orientation (vertical vs. horizontal) on the ultrasonic fatigue performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V and Inconel 718.
summary_en.method: Ultrasonic fatigue testing at 20 kHz was performed on five specimens per orientation per alloy, supported by Digital Image Correlation (DIC), laser measurements, and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to characterize mechanical and fatigue behavior.
summary_en.result: Horizontally built specimens exhibited longer fatigue lives and higher stiffness along the loading axis, confirming orientation-dependent anisotropy.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing including ultrasonic fatigue and DIC, combined with FEA, provided validation of the stress and deformation behavior.
